modern: For this is the truth of it, men of Athens: wherever a man has placed himself, thinking it the best place for him, or has been placed by a commander, there in my opinion he ought to stay and face the risk, taking nothing into account, either death or anything else, before the shame of deserting his post.
original: For thus it is, men of Athens, in truth: wherever a man has placed himself thinking it the best place for him, or has been placed by a commander, there in my opinion he ought to stay and to abide the hazard, taking nothing into the reckoning, either death or anything else, before the baseness [of deserting his post].
notification: For this is the truth of it, men of Athens…
notification_original: For thus it is, men of Athens, in truth…

explained.summary:
More from Socrates’ defence speech. Wherever you’ve taken your stand, because you judged it best or because a commander put you there, you should stay and face the danger, counting neither death nor anything else as worse than the disgrace of deserting your post.

For Marcus, an emperor stuck on the frontier at war, this was not abstract. His post was the empire, and he meant to hold it.
explained.today: Staying with a hard job because people depend on you, caring for an ailing parent when it would be easier to step back, or speaking up in a meeting when silence would be safer are all versions of holding your post.
